title: Psalms Chapter 78 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 78 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 78 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 78.

questions.question: What should the people do according to Psalms 78:1?
options: Ignore the words of my mouth
questions.explanation: In Psalms 78:1, the psalmist urges the people to listen to his law, indicating the importance of paying attention to divine instruction.

questions.question: What does the psalmist intend to open his mouth in, according to Psalms 78:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:2 states that the psalmist will open his mouth in a parable, indicating he will convey deeper truths through stories.

questions.question: Who are the 'children' referred to in Psalms 78:6?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 78:6, the reference to 'children' pertains to the next generation of Israelites who should learn the ways of God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 78:7, what should the people set their hope in?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:7 indicates that the people should set their hope in God and not forget his works.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Ephraim are described as turning back in battle in Psalms 78:9.
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:9 describes the children of Ephraim as being armed but turning back in the day of battle, indicating their failure to stand firm.

questions.question: What did the people do to provoke God in the wilderness according to Psalms 78:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:17 states that the people sinned against God by provoking the most High in the wilderness.

questions.question: True or False: God rained down manna upon the people according to Psalms 78:24.
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 78:24, God rained down manna upon the people to eat, showcasing his provision for them.

questions.question: What did the people ask for in Psalms 78:18?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 78:18, the people provoked God by asking for meat for their lust, indicating their dissatisfaction with what God provided.

questions.question: According to Psalms 78:21, what was the LORD's reaction to the people's words?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:21 states that the LORD was wroth, indicating his anger at the people's lack of faith and trust in Him.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:11 say the people did to the works of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:11 indicates that the people forgat his works and wonders, demonstrating their lack of remembrance of God's actions.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist instructs not to hide God's praises from children in Psalms 78:4.
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:4 emphasizes that praises of the LORD should not be hidden from children, highlighting the importance of teaching future generations.

questions.question: In Psalms 78:12, where did God perform marvelous things?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:12 refers to the marvelous things done by God in the sight of the fathers in the land of Egypt.

questions.question: In Psalms 78, what comes FIRST in the instructions given?
options: To not forget the works of God
To give ear to my law
To show praises to the next generation
questions.correctAnswer: To give ear to my law
questions.explanation: The first instruction in Psalms 78 is to give ear to my law (Psalms 78:1), which sets the foundation for the other instructions.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 78 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 78 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What food did God provide for His people in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Man did eat angels' food: he sent them meat to the full.' (Psalms 78:25) This indicates that the food provided was remarkable, described as 'angels' food.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 78, what did God cause to blow in the heavens?
questions.explanation: The text mentions that 'He caused an east wind to blow in the heaven: and by his power he brought in the south wind.' (Psalms 78:26) This shows God's control over nature.

questions.question: What did God send down upon His people in the wilderness as described in Psalms 78?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He rained flesh also upon them as dust, and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.' (Psalms 78:27) This illustrates God's provision for His people's needs.

questions.question: How did the people respond to the abundance provided by God?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates, 'For all this they sinned still, and believed not for his wondrous works.' (Psalms 78:32) This shows a lack of faith in God's provision.

questions.question: What was the consequence of the people's sin according to Psalms 78?
options: Their days were consumed in vanity
questions.correctAnswer: Their days were consumed in vanity
questions.explanation: The scripture states, 'Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble.' (Psalms 78:33) This highlights the serious consequences of their unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What did the people remember when they sought God after being punished?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.' (Psalms 78:35) This reflects their realization of God's sustaining power.

questions.question: True or False: God was quick to anger with the Israelites for their lack of faith.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Therefore the LORD heard this, and was wroth...' (Psalms 78:21) indicates that God was indeed angered by their lack of faith.

questions.question: True or False: The people remembered the signs God performed in Egypt.
questions.explanation: The text states, 'They remembered not his hand, nor the day when he delivered them from the enemy.' (Psalms 78:42), indicating they forgot His past deliverance.

questions.question: What did God do to the firstborn in Egypt according to Psalms 78?
questions.explanation: The scripture states, 'And smote all the firstborn in Egypt; the chief of their strength in the tabernacles of Ham.' (Psalms 78:51) This was a judgment against Egypt.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:38 tell us about God's character?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But he, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not...' (Psalms 78:38), emphasizing God's compassion despite their sin.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:40 highlight about the Israelites' behavior?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'How oft did they provoke him in the wilderness, and grieve him in the desert!' (Psalms 78:40), highlighting their repeated rebellion against God.

questions.question: What lesson can we learn from the Israelites' experience regarding trust in God?
options: Lack of trust leads to judgment
Remembering God's past works is unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Lack of trust leads to judgment
questions.explanation: The context shows that their disbelief and inability to trust in God's provision led to severe consequences (Psalms 78:21, 32).

questions.question: How does Psalms 78 teach us about remembering God's works?
questions.explanation: The psalm encourages recounting God's faithfulness and miraculous deeds to foster trust and hope in future provision (Psalms 78:4-7).

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 78 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 78.

questions.question: What did the psalmist intend to show to the generation to come?
questions.explanation: The psalmist intended to show the praises of the LORD, his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done, as stated in Psalms 78:4.

questions.question: Which generation is described as stubborn and rebellious in Psalms 78?
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes the generation that did not set their heart aright and whose spirit was not stedfast with God as a stubborn and rebellious generation in Psalms 78:8.

questions.question: What did God do in the land of Egypt according to Psalms 78?
options: He led them with a cloud
questions.explanation: The psalmist recounts the wonders God performed in Egypt, including turning rivers into blood and sending divers sorts of flies, as indicated in Psalms 78:43-45.

questions.question: How did the people respond after God delivered them from Egypt?
questions.explanation: Despite God's wonders, the psalmist notes that they sinned still and believed not for his wondrous works, as stated in Psalms 78:32.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:39 say about God's perception of humanity?
questions.explanation: The verse states that God remembered they were but flesh; a wind that passeth away and cometh not again, emphasizing human frailty in Psalms 78:39.

questions.question: In Psalms 78, who did God choose to lead His people?
questions.explanation: The psalmist highlights that God chose David his servant to lead His people, as mentioned in Psalms 78:70.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel remembered the day when God delivered them from the enemy.
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that they remembered not his hand, nor the day when he delivered them from the enemy, as stated in Psalms 78:42.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Psalms 78 to convey its messages?
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions he will open his mouth in a parable and utter dark sayings of old in Psalms 78:2, indicating the use of parables.

questions.question: Which tribe did God refuse, according to Psalms 78?
questions.explanation: The psalmist notes that God refused the tabernacle of Joseph and chose not the tribe of Ephraim in Psalms 78:67.

questions.question: What did God provide to the Israelites in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: God provided water from the rock, manna from heaven, and led them with a cloud and fire, as described throughout Psalms 78:15-24.

questions.question: How did the psalmist describe the actions of the people towards God?
questions.explanation: The psalmist notes that they tempted and provoked the most high God, and kept not his testimonies, as stated in Psalms 78:56.

questions.question: True or False: God was angry with Israel for their unfaithfulness.
questions.explanation: God was indeed angry with Israel for provoking Him and for not keeping His testimonies, as indicated in Psalms 78:59.

questions.question: What Hebrew word describes God's anger in Psalms 78:49?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Za'am' is often used to describe God's fierce anger and indignation, as reflected in Psalms 78:49.

questions.question: In Psalms 78, what did God do to the firstborn of Egypt?
questions.explanation: The psalmist recounts that God smote all the firstborn in Egypt, as stated in Psalms 78:51.

questions.question: What did God do for His people in the wilderness according to Psalms 78:52?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that God made his own people go forth like sheep and guided them in the wilderness like a flock, as seen in Psalms 78:52.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 78 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 78 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:4 emphasize regarding the transmission of God's works?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:4 states, 'We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done.' This emphasizes the importance of passing down knowledge of God's deeds to future generations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 78:10, what did the children of Ephraim fail to do?
options: Follow the law of the land
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:10 states, 'They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law;' showing their failure to maintain their commitment to God.

questions.question: What miraculous event does Psalms 78:13 recount?
options: The parting of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: The parting of the Red Sea
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:13 says, 'He divided the sea, and caused them to pass through; and he made the waters to stand as an heap.' This directly refers to the miraculous parting of the Red Sea during the Exodus.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:19 illustrate about the Israelites' attitude in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:19 states, 'Yea, they spake against God; they said, Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?' This reflects their lack of faith and trust in God's provision.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:22 reveal about the Israelites' faith?
options: They were faithful to His commands
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:22 states, 'Because they believed not in God, and trusted not in his salvation:' indicating a lack of faith among the Israelites.

questions.question: What attribute of God is displayed in Psalms 78:38?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:38 says, 'But he, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not:' showcasing God's compassionate nature towards His people.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'a stubborn and rebellious generation' in Psalms 78:8 refer to?
options: The generation that came after Joshua
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:8 describes 'a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright' referring to the Israelites during their time in the wilderness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:39 illustrate about humanity's nature?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:39 states, 'For he remembered that they were but flesh; a wind that passeth away, and cometh not again.' This highlights the frailty and transient nature of human life.

questions.question: In Psalms 78:53, how does God guide His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:53 states, 'But made his own people to go forth like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock,' illustrating God's protective and guiding nature.

questions.question: What significant event is described in Psalms 78:51?
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:51 recounts, 'And smote all the firstborn in Egypt; the chief of their strength in the tabernacles of Ham:' referring to the final plague during the Exodus.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:57 indicate about the Israelites' behavior?
options: They turned back and dealt unfaithfully
questions.correctAnswer: They turned back and dealt unfaithfully
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:57 states, 'But turned back, and dealt unfaithfully like their fathers: they were turned aside like a deceitful bow,' highlighting their unfaithfulness to God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:68 reveal about God's choice of tribe?
options: He chose the tribe of Ephraim
He chose the tribe of Judah
He chose the tribe of Levi
He chose the tribe of Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: He chose the tribe of Judah
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:68 states, 'But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.' This indicates God's selection of Judah for a special purpose.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5-6 and verse 11 convey about God's commandments?
options: They are meant to be taught to children
questions.correctAnswer: They are meant to be taught to children
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 emphasize the establishment of a testimony and law for teaching future generations, while verse 11 highlights the forgetting of God's works, indicating the importance of teaching His commandments.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is untrustworthy in His promises. What does Psalms 78:23-24 actually teach?
options: God does not provide for His people
God commands the clouds and provides manna
questions.correctAnswer: God commands the clouds and provides manna
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:23-24 teaches that God 'had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, And had rained down manna upon them to eat,' demonstrating His faithfulness in provision and fulfillment of promises.

questions.question: What does Psalms 78:72 reveal about God's leadership style?
options: He leads with integrity and skillfulness
questions.correctAnswer: He leads with integrity and skillfulness
questions.explanation: Psalms 78:72 states, 'So he fed them according to the integrity of his heart; and guided them by the skilfulness of his hands,' indicating God's righteous and skillful leadership.
